claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me start with a few questions.

**First, could you tell me the names and ages of all the children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: **Are you a UK resident, and do you have responsibility for Alex?** For example, do you live with Alex and provide for them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives with me at home. I'm responsible for looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

**Next, I'd like to know: Are you currently working or receiving any income? If so, could you tell me roughly what your annual income is?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am working, yes. My annual income is around £55,000.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's useful to know.

**One more question: Is Alex in full-time education or training?** For example, is Alex attending school full-time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in school full-time - just at primary school at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided:
- You live in the UK and have responsibility for Alex
- Alex is 8 years old and in full-time education at primary school
- Your annual income is around £55,000

Let me now determine your eligibility status.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex meets all the qualifying conditions:
- Alex is 8 years old (under the age limit of 16)
- Alex is in full-time education at primary school
- You are a UK resident with parental responsibility for Alex
- You live together

**Important note about your income:** Your income of approximately £55,000 means you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge. This is a tax charge that applies when income exceeds £50,000, but it doesn't make you ineligible for Child Benefit itself. Instead, it means you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return. You may want to seek advice from HMRC or a tax professional about how this affects you specifically.

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
